# `prefer-testing-expect-error`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports a manual catch-based assertion for one expected error.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`expectError` states the test contract directly and reports unexpected success
or a different error clearly.

## When it fires

It applies to `operation() catch |err| { try std.testing.expectEqual(error.E,
err); return; };` followed by `return error.TestExpectedError;` as the last two
statements of a function or test body. A handler that does anything else, such
as passing `error.OutOfMemory` through for an allocation-failure sweep or
asserting more state, leaves through a labeled `break`, or sits in a nested
block (where its `return` skips later statements) is not equivalent and is not
reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn lookup() !void {
    return error.NotFound;
}

test "lookup fails" {
    lookup() catch |err| {
        try std.testing.expectEqual(error.NotFound, err);
        return;
    };
    return error.TestExpectedError;
}
```
